subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes, unit economics & renewal step-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>; Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + pricing next steps

Hi Samantha — great to meet today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call:

- Estimated monthly tokens: 1.2M baseline, with spikes up to ~3.5M for campaign windows.
- Primary use case: customer support triage + auto-summaries (short prompts, avg 120 tokens/input, 300 tokens/output).
- Performance needs: P95 latency < 500ms for UI flows; batch/async ok for non-critical work.

Pricing & qualification items we agreed to validate:
- Target unit economics: trying to land around $700–$1,000 per 1M tokens for blended usage across chat + summarization.
- Budget range: $15k–$40k/mo initially; open to ramp/commit for discounted tiers.

Next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) Marissa: Send a model for pricing banding (per-1M token) + simple step-up schedule for renewal/expansion (today).
2) Samantha: Confirm expected monthly seasonality and whether embeddings will be billed separately (by Tue).
3) Procurement: Share SSO/PO cadence and any procurement windows that would affect the SOW (this week).

Attaching a quick pricing workbook with tiered examples and a draft SOW for procurement to review. Happy to hop on another call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-pricing-1m-5m.xlsx, SOW-draft-Acme-2026.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + pricing next steps

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tokens: the 1.2M is the conservative baseline; expected steady-state after Q3 is ~2.8M. We have one large seasonal window in Nov-Dec that could hit 5–6M in a month.
- Embeddings: yes, we will need embeddings for search and reranking — call that out as a separate usage line item.
- Budget: procurement has set an initial committed budget of $25k/mo, with potential to expand to $45k/mo after Q3 if SLAs and cost look good.

Can you share an example blended rate if we commit to 3M avg / 12M annual? Also, procurement asked for any committed discount thresholds and what the blended outcome would look like if we add an extra route/model with higher token usage.

Samantha
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp
samantha.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + pricing next steps

Great — thanks for the visibility, Samantha. Attached is a short workbook with three scenarios:

A) Conservatively committed: 1M tokens/mo baseline (annual commit 12M)
B) Mid ramp: 3M tokens/mo avg (annual 36M) — likely your expected steady-state
C) Expansion: 6M tokens/mo peak season with annualized blended 30M–40M

Key highlights from the workbook (sheet: blended_rates):
- Example blended per-1M token rates (chat+summarization, standard models):
  • Scenario A: $1,200 / 1M tokens
  • Scenario B: $820 / 1M tokens (base volume discount kicks in at 25M annual)
  • Scenario C: $520 / 1M tokens (volume step-ups + committed uplift)
- Embeddings: quoted separately at $75 / 100k embedding vectors (or equivalent $750 / 1M embedding tokens depending on embed size).
- Adding a high-throughput route/model (e.g., larger context summarizer) changes the blended mix — example shows blended moving +10–15% if that route is 30% of tokens but priced at +20% per-1M.

Recommended path: Start with a 12–month commit at mid-ramp (36M annual) with a Q4 true-up clause (seasonal cap) and an option to add a second route at a pre-agreed blended uplift. This yields an example target around $800 / 1M blended in year-1.

I've flagged the procurement questions in the SOW draft; Dev, can you confirm expected SLA targets and whether Dedicated capacity is needed for the initial phase? Rishi — looping you for renewal/step-up cadence and approval on the proposed step-tier pricing.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-pricing-1m-5m.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + pricing next steps

Hi team — quick technical note from infra side:

- For 3M avg with occasional 6M peaks, our hosted platform should meet latency SLOs with default autoscaling. No Dedicated capacity required initially unless Acme needs strict tenancy or additional throughput guarantees.
- If you commit to a reserved tier / Dedicated, we can offer tighter P95 SLOs and a further 5–10% discount on blended rates.

I'll add suggested SLA language to the SOW and call out any provisioning lead times (2–4 weeks for Dedicated pools).

—Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes, unit economics & renewal step-ups

Samantha — thanks for sharing budget and seasonality. A few commercial notes from the renewals lens:

- Step-up schedule proposal (example):
  • Year 1 commit: 36M tokens annual @ $820 / 1M (blended)
  • Year 2 target: 60M annual with pre-negotiated step tiers bringing blended to ~$620 / 1M
  • True-up and review each Q4; auto-apply step discounts if thresholds hit.
- Blended math: we'll produce a simple uplift model that shows per-route rates and a blended line you can use for internal forecasting.
- Adding new route/models: propose a "route addendum" process that locks in the per-route pricing for the remainder of the contract period to avoid surprise blended swings.

Next step: Marissa to send the final workbook and SOW for procurement review; if procurement is comfortable we can prepare a Term Sheet for signature next week.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
